thread_title: Getting S. 'Elaine Wang' in TC, and suggestions?
breadcrumb: Getting S. 'Elaine Wang' in TC, and suggestions?

posts.body_html:
Many of you have been jonesii'ing for a piece of S. 'Elaine Wang' and I've been working very hard to get this thing invitro for over a year now. Challenge is, for a patent to be granted, you can't distribute the plant to anyone else.

So far, Agristarts rejected the offer (they didn't get back to me after several attempts) and Rancho Tissue Technologies in Southern California said they would, but require $8,000.00! It's ironic because for everything else, there is no fee, they just pay you royalties once they start selling the material. From their website:

"Once a new plant is submitted to us, our technicians evaluate it to see if RTT can effectively tissue culture the plant. If so, RTT will begin the tissue process. RTT will pay a royalty to the breeder or collector for each plant we sell. RTT has strong ties with brokers and wholesalers throughout the world to be certain your plant is properly promoted."


Does anyone have suggestions?

Mike I know you are pretty knowledgeable about tc. Is it possible that you could bootstrap yourself the rest of the way and crack the sarracenia tc code? I'm sure it would take some serious time, but if you put the right clones in tc, perhaps it might pay off, plus get a lot of sarrs out into greater circulation?

I'm guessing the key must lie in some sort of pre-treatment where all of the internal critters are killed in-situ before a specimen is prepped for the tc jar.
